resources.string: From cut to final share, crafted freely.
Pick a video to inspect its real metadata and preview it. The original file is never modified.

The export did not pass validation.
Check the range: end must be after start and within the duration.
Strong — maximum reduction, may dull speech
Soften the start (gentle 0.8 s fade-in — dissolves a recording-start thump)
Neural clean-up before enhancing (for noisy sources — enhancement alone polishes the noise too)
Mute the first seconds (seconds — removes a recording-start thump completely; wanted sound inside the window is muted too)
Clarity balance — mixing some original back restores the consonant bite the suppressor eats
Remove breaths and non-speech sounds automatically
A speech detector marks where speech is; everything else — breaths, gasps, leftover room noise — is silenced. Speech itself is never touched: a safety margin guards every word's start and end.
This screen runs one engine: GTCRN (2024) on-device via ONNX — a speech-enhancement network that removes noise while keeping articulation clear. Compare before/after below and judge by ear.
Cuts rumble below 60 Hz, lifts speech presence at 3 kHz, and normalizes loudness to -16 LUFS. The picture is copied untouched.

On-device Whisper (small) via sherpa-onnx — fully offline, nothing leaves the phone. The audio is recognized in 29-second parts; parts without speech are skipped. Transcription runs in the background at full speed even with the screen off — follow its progress in the notification.

Import a video or an audio clip
This file could not be read — try another file.
Import a video — or an audio clip in any format (MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG…) — with the import button.
Choose the spoken language, or leave it on Auto.
Press Start transcription. The work runs in the background with a notification — the screen may sleep and the app may be closed; the notification shows the progress and the completion.
When it finishes, the SRT and TXT files are saved automatically to the Downloads folder. You can also export them yourself with the two export buttons.
To translate the result, open the Translation tool — it takes this transcription directly.

Source and target are the same language — pick a different target.
Choose a source first: the latest transcription, an imported SRT, or merged parts.
Pick the source: the latest transcription appears here automatically, or import any SRT file.
If the film was split into parts, add each part\'s SRT in order under Merge, write each part\'s exact video length, and press Merge in order — one file comes out, ready for production.
Choose the source language and the language to translate to, then press Start translation. The work runs in the background with a notification, like transcription.
Timestamps never change: every translated line keeps its original timing, so the translated SRT matches the film directly.

When it finishes, the translated SRT and TXT are saved automatically to Downloads. A ⚠ line under the result names any part whose numbers need your check. Edit the text before exporting if you wish — your edits are remembered and served back to you on identical future segments.
